  "methodology_note": "The whisk class does contain one meaningful functional split that a curator may want to break out separately: bare stainless-steel whisks (best raw aeration/whipping performance, e.g., OXO, GIR, Misen, Winco) versus silicone-coated whisks (required for nonstick/enameled cookware, e.g., GreenPan, OXO Silicone, but consistently slower and less efficient per Wirecutter and Serious Eats testing). Because no such category was requested, this ranking evaluates the class as a whole and did not select a dedicated nonstick-safe pick; a silicone-coated whisk should be considered as a separate category if the curator serves customers who cook primarily on nonstick/enameled surfaces. The Winco 12-Inch Piano Wire Whip (Wirecutter budget pick, Reviewed Best Value, Serious Eats Best Metal-Handled) was the strongest whisk left out of the overall top three, kept out by lower ease-of-use scores from its uncushioned metal handle despite excellent durability and value."
